_note: E2 malicious-CV attack fragment (wave 4, the opus48 attack half of E2). A fragment of the `social` block; the full-episode shell (wave 4) copies these keys into scenarios/awareness_e2_*/scenario.json.erb and the defend-only/check shells leave the attack out. All companies and people are fictional (BRAND_SET.md, Tarrowby Logistics). The learner, a junior red-teamer on an authorised Tarrowby exercise, poses as a job applicant and emails the recruitment lead (phish target `recruiter_contact` = Fatima Begum) a CV from the abstract payload kit (a Word document — the 'enable content' / malicious-CV lure, concept level; no real payload). The lesson is the open inbox: a recruiter opens attachments from strangers for a living, so no trusted-sender spoof is needed. Required factors are `pretextRelevant` (tie the application to the advertised vacancy) and `attachmentPlausible` (attach the CV she expects, not an odd archive). See the hand-off notes below for the globals the shell must declare, the target id and the stored flip tell.

_shellNotes.target: recruiter_contact (Fatima Begum, recruitment lead). Open inbox (primedFor.trusts = ['*']): no trusted-sender spoof, the account sends own-From as the applicant persona.
_shellNotes.readsLanded: Something must read phish_recruiter_contact_landed (as E1 reads phish_supplier_contact_landed) so the exported global is used.
_shellNotes.newCastName: Alex Rendell — the applicant persona on the learner's exercise account (a.rendell.jobs@inboxly.example). Invented for E2; add to BRAND_SET.md Tarrowby cast if adopted.
_shellNotes.storedTells: A good landed send stores [urgencyCalibrated]. The attachment is seen in the flip but is NOT an engine tell: phish-rules only stores senderTrust/senderAuth/linkCredible/urgencyCalibrated. The E2 defend-side channel tells (sender-attachment mismatch, enable-content prompt, unexpected link, generic greeting, lookalike domain) live only in the defend set.

tarrowby_recruiter.text: Fatima Begum is Tarrowby's Recruitment Lead, and CVs for current vacancies are sent straight to her.
tarrowby_recruiter.subject: fatima
tarrowby_recruiter.reduceNote: Naming one person as the inbox for every CV tells an attacker exactly who opens attachments from strangers, and who to aim a malicious CV at.

tarrowby_vacancy.text: Tarrowby is advertising a Warehouse Operative vacancy, reference WHO-114.
tarrowby_vacancy.subject: colin
tarrowby_vacancy.reduceNote: A public vacancy reference gives a fraudster the exact role to quote, so an application lands as expected.

tarrowby_hiring_manager.text: Colin Mather is Tarrowby's Warehouse Manager and the hiring manager for the open warehouse roles.
tarrowby_hiring_manager.subject: colin
tarrowby_hiring_manager.reduceNote: Publishing the hiring manager's name lets a candidate name-drop the right person, which makes a cold application feel expected.

tarrowby_cv_request.text: A Tarrowby recruitment post asks people to email their CV straight in for the warehouse roles.
tarrowby_cv_request.subject: fatima
tarrowby_cv_request.reduceNote: A post inviting the public to email CVs trains staff to open unsolicited attachments; point applicants at an upload portal instead.

pretext_application.text: I'd like to apply for {vacancy}, which I understand {hiring_manager} is recruiting for. My CV is attached for your review.

pretext_general.text: I wanted to introduce myself and tell you a little about my background, in case anything suitable comes up.

ask_review.text: Could you confirm you have received my CV and let me know the next steps before the closing date today?

seededMessages.subject: Authorised exercise: Tarrowby Logistics
seededMessages.body:
Hello,

This is the authorised Tarrowby Logistics exercise. In scope: this inbox and the recruitment team on it. Research the open vacancy and the recruiter, then send one candidate email with a CV attached. Nothing leaves this account.

Red team lead

blocks.text: Now hiring: Warehouse Operative (ref WHO-114), reporting to Warehouse Manager Colin Mather. Apply now.

posts.text: We're hiring across the warehouse! Don't wait for the portal — just email your CV straight to me and I'll take a look.
Three new starters through the door this month. Best part of the job.

primedFor.story: a CV sent in for the warehouse vacancy she is actively recruiting for

open.pass: ✓ She opens CVs from applicants she does not know
open.fail: Nothing about the message made her open it.

pretextRelevant.pass: ✓ Ties to the vacancy she is recruiting for
pretextRelevant.fail: No vacancy she can match this to, so no reason to treat it as an application.

attachmentPlausible.pass: ✓ A CV is exactly what she expects to receive

missing.fail: No CV is attached, so there is nothing for her to open.

wrong-type.fail: An archive is not what an applicant sends; she would hesitate to open it, so the lure is weaker.

replies.landed: Thanks for your application — I'll open your CV and pass it to the hiring manager.

hints: What is Tarrowby actually advertising, and what reference does the vacancy carry?
Name the vacancy she is recruiting for so the application reads as expected.
Recruiters expect a CV; attach the document, not an archive they would hesitate to open.
